title: OWASP Top 10: Injection (SQLi), XSS & Cookie Hardening
summary: Prevent SQL Injection via prepared bindings, sanitize XSS outputs alongside CSP headers, and harden HttpOnly/SameSite session cookies.
learningObjectives: Neutralize SQL Injection using parameterized queries rather than brittle string blacklisting
Defend browsers against Stored/Reflected XSS and CSRF via escaping, CSP, and hardened cookie attributes
prerequisiteConcepts: Basic HTML DOM and SQL SELECT knowledge

sections.heading: 1. Separating Code From Data (Injection & XSS)
sections.content:
Both SQL Injection (SQLi) and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) trace to the same architectural root failure: mixing untrusted user text directly into parsed code grammars (SQL parsers on servers or JavaScript HTML parsers in browsers).

Defeating SQLi demands parameterized prepared statements (`SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = $1`, passing inputs out-of-band as bound literal parameters). Defeating XSS combines automatic contextual framework escaping (`{userBio}` in React rather than `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`), strict input sanitization (`DOMPurify` when rich HTML is intentionally allowed), and a strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP) blocking arbitrary inline script execution.

codeExamples.code:
[Unsafe]      "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name='" + input + "'"  -> Parser merges input into SQL!
[Safe]        "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1"  + [$1]    -> DB treats $1 strictly as data!
[Hardened]    Set-Cookie: session=...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
codeExamples.explanation: Prepared bindings keep user bytes completely inert regardless of quotes or semicolons, while cookie flags guard sessions.

keyPoints: Never rely on regex blacklists stripping `--` or `'SELECT'`—bypassed easily via encoding or casing tricks.
`HttpOnly` stops `document.cookie` JS theft during any XSS flaw; `SameSite=Lax` mitigates cross-site CSRF.
commonMistakes: Storing sensitive JWT tokens inside `localStorage` where third-party scripts or XSS read them effortlessly.

sections.heading: 2. Defensive Coding Comparison & CSP Header
sections.content: Compare parameterized DB lookups alongside defensive Content Security Policy headers below.

codeExamples.explanation: Passing `[submittedEmail]` as `$1` binds parameters strictly as inert strings while CSP `frame-ancestors 'none'` stops clickjacking.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Immunity to SQLi injection payloads combined with strict browser XSS/Clickjacking protection

keyPoints: Combine contextual output encoding with `HttpOnly` + `Secure` + `SameSite` cookies.
commonMistakes: Inserting untrusted `href` URLs starting with `javascript:alert(1)` inside React `<a href={userUrl}>` without protocol allowlist (`http:`/`https:`).

exercises.title: Neutralize SQLi & XSS in User Profile Component
exercises.objective: Convert raw SQL concatenation and dangerous URL bindings into safe patterns.
exercises.description: Refactor a query interpolating `searchTerm` and a profile link rendering `<a href={website}>` safely without allowing `javascript:` URIs.
instructions: Convert `SELECT * FROM courses WHERE title LIKE '%${term}%'` to positional `$1` parameterized form.
Validate `website` URL parses cleanly with `new URL()` permitting strictly `https:` or `http:` protocols.
hints: `const parsed = new URL(url); return parsed.protocol === 'https:' || parsed.protocol === 'http:';`
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: Positional `$1` binds `%${term}%` cleanly, and `new URL()` protocol allowlisting blocks `javascript:` href payload execution.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why do `HttpOnly` session cookies outperform `localStorage` tokens against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)?

options.text: `HttpOnly` cookies cannot be read via browser `document.cookie` JavaScript, stopping XSS payloads from exfiltrating the raw token

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Isolating credentials away from JS DOM scope blunts token theft.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What happens if an attacker enters `' OR '1'='1` into an application using parameterized queries (`WHERE email = $1`)?

options.text: The database safely looks for an exact literal email matching `' OR '1'='1` and returns zero rows without running boolean OR logic
The attacker logs in automatically as Admin
Node throws an unhandled promise panic

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Parameterized variables are never parsed as SQL keywords or operators.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Which CSP directive blocks attackers from embedding your application inside hidden malicious iframes (Clickjacking defense)?

recap: You neutralized SQLi with prepared bindings, guarded href/DOM sinks against XSS, and locked down browser cookies cleanly.
